text:
Liam Chen: seeing a weird scale-up lag in us-east1 during the morning spike, requests queueing >10s. Autoscaler shows 0 pending scale events even though pending pods = 120
infra-bot: alert: provisioner-heartbeat-mismatch detected for cluster-us-east1 at 2035001220 (checked by heartbeat-monitor) :warning:
Maya Rivera: logs? could be the provisioner not registering instances with the coordinator or redis TTLs expiring
Liam Chen: pasting the redis state we pulled from the coordinator host (shortened):
```
127.0.0.1:6379> KEYS provisioner:us-east1:nodes*
1) "provisioner:us-east1:nodes:node-73"
2) "provisioner:us-east1:nodes:node-74"
127.0.0.1:6379> TTL provisioner:us-east1:nodes:node-73
(integer) -2  # key exists but no TTL (we use TTL for liveness)
127.0.0.1:6379> GET provisioner:us-east1:heartbeat_offset
"3600"
```
Priya Shah: whoa heartbeat_offset=3600s? expected <30s. That explains why coordinator thinks nodes are stale/unregistered. Where did that offset come from?
Ken Patel: looks like an unintentional cron on the provisioner host swapped timezones and a startup flag defaulted HEARTBEAT_OFFSET=3600. We shipped a container image change yesterday that added a config fallback.
Maya Rivera: autoscaler relies on coordinator's live node set. If nodes appear stale, autoscaler will throttle scale actions to avoid oscillation -> scale-up lag. That matches the 0 pending scale events.
Liam Chen: rolling a quick fix: bump coordinator to ignore heartbeat_offset > 60s and restart provisioner process on a single node to verify. I'll run the command: `kubectl -n infra rollout restart deploy/provisioner-us-east1`
infra-bot: deploy/provisioner-us-east1 restart initiated by liam (k8s event 2035001252)
Priya Shah: also adding a temporary traffic shift: move 30% of new traffic away from us-east1 to us-west1 via traffic-allocator to reduce pressure while we stabilize. I'll flip weighted routing in Route53 and the edge proxy.
Liam Chen: fix applied on provisioner: set HEARTBEAT_OFFSET=30 in configmap and restarted. Coordinator now showing TTLs present:
```
127.0.0.1:6379> TTL provisioner:us-east1:nodes:node-73
(integer) 22
```
Maya Rivera: autoscaler started enqueuing scale events ~20s after restart. We're seeing new nodes provisioning, but some are spot instances; QA: what's the expected cost hit if we keep the fallback on for 2h?
Ken Patel: rough estimate: fallback spot backfill ~ 25 GPUs @ $0.12/hr = $72/hr. If we reserve Dedicated spare for 2h it's ~ $300/hr — spots cheaper but risk evictions.
Priya Shah: opted for mixed: leave spot backfill enabled for now, enable fast retry to provision reserved if spot eviction rate >10% in next 15m.
Liam Chen: monitoring shows p95 latency dropping back to baseline within 4m. Autoscaler churn halted, no thrash.
infra-bot: incident note auto-created: provisioner-heartbeat-offset-us-east1, severity=sev2, owners=[eng-infra] (2035001299)
Maya Rivera: postmortem items: 1) validate config fallback doesn't produce large offsets, 2) add unit test for heartbeat offset bounds, 3) add alert for heartbeat_offset > 60s, 4) run a small chaos test to ensure autoscaler behaves when coordinator liveness toggles.
Ken Patel: assigning followups on the board, will sync with finance about the spot cost delta for the incident.
Liam Chen: thanks all. Leaving traffic-weight at 70/30 until we confirm stable for 30m, then revert.
Priya Shah: noted, will revert route when stable. :thumbsup:
Maya Rivera: adding a short summary for infra-oncall channel and tagging eng-sre for visibility.
